newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary's BUX ends lower after Fed's decision.
newsitem.headline: Hungary's BUX ends lower after Fed's decision.

text.p: Hungarian shares closed mixed on Wednesday, remaining unaffected by the fact that the U.S. Fed left interest rates unchanged, traders said.
The BUX index closed at a preliminary 5,848.20 points, down 39.55 points or 0.67 percent.

"The market was mixed, with MOL shadowing the overall picture by its fall," one trader said. "The Dow closed higher on Tuesday, while the dollar was weaker and these factors more or less offset each other."

MOL suffered a loss of 80 forints to close at 3,300 as the market's speculations have been settling after the completion of the second phase of its privatisation and the release of its first quarter earnings.
Traders added MOL might see limited falls from next week on as domestic investors were likely to begin to unload MOL papers they had bought in the domestic public offer.
"I doubt it would fall to the level of the issue price (2,970 forints) but it can easily lose another 100 forints from its current level," a trader said.
Others expect the market to enter a calmer phase once the second phase of privatisation in pharmaceuticals Richter Gedeon Rt is completed later this month.

"If subscriptions in Richter are over, there will be hardly any news about the country," said Peter Nagy of Postabank Securities. "I don't expect the market to move upwards in the coming period as it lacks momentum."
BUX futures well reflect this, Nagy said, adding that a drop on the cash market is coupled usually by more substantial falls on the futures.
On Wednesday BUX futures settlement prices fell by between 100 and 239 points.
On the cash market OTP Bank shares rose 35 forints to 4,310, while chemical manufacturer Borsodchem firmed 40 forints to 6,490.
Pharmaceuticals Egis edged up 50 to 10,850 and chemicals TVK put on five forints to end at 2,685.
Retailer Fotex strengthened almost three percent to end at 140 forints, apparently benefiting from its Q1 earnings, Nagy said.
